Marsh Wren shows buffy sides that blend into whitish central underparts.
Marsh Wren has a pale throat that is cleaner and less brown than the surrounding face.
Marsh Wren shows a dark upperpart panel across the back broken by narrow white lines.
Marsh Wren has a more boldly patterned back than House Wren and Winter Wren.
Marsh Wren shows a darker and more contrasting back pattern than Rock Wren.
Marsh Wren has a less dramatic facial stripe pattern than Bewick Wren but a much more patterned back.
Marsh Wren shows warm brown wings and tail set against a black-streaked back.
Marsh Wren has a tail that is both short and distinctly barred, unlike the plainer look of House Wren.
Marsh Wren shows the combination of a pale eyebrow, black-and-white streaked back, and warm buff underparts.

Winter Wren shows dense dark barring across the back, unlike the mostly plain back of House Wren.
Winter Wren has narrow black barring across the folded wings that is stronger than on House Wren or Carolina Wren.
Winter Wren shows a strongly barred tail, not the more simply patterned tail of House Wren.
Winter Wren has heavy dark barring on the flanks, creating a more patterned look than House Wren.
Winter Wren shows barring over the back, wings, tail, and flanks together, giving a much more densely marked appearance than House Wren.
Winter Wren has an extremely short tail that looks shorter than the tail of House Wren.
Winter Wren often shows a sharply cocked tail that appears more stubby than in Carolina Wren.
Winter Wren has a tail that looks noticeably shorter than the folded wing.
Winter Wren shows a compact, round-bodied shape with a tiny tail and broad chest.
Winter Wren has rich rufous-brown upperparts rather than the brighter chestnut tones and bold face pattern of Carolina Wren.
Winter Wren shows a plain brown face without the bold facial contrast seen on Carolina Wren or Bewick Wren.
Winter Wren has only a very short, weak pale eyebrow, unlike the long bold white eyebrow of Marsh Wren.
Winter Wren shows only a faint supercilium, much less obvious than in Carolina Wren.
Winter Wren has a weak, short eyebrow rather than the crisp long eyebrow of Bewick Wren.
Winter Wren shows no bold white throat patch, unlike Carolina Wren.
Winter Wren has underparts washed buff-brown rather than strongly contrasting pale below as in Bewick Wren.
Winter Wren shows a throat that blends softly into the breast instead of standing out white.
Winter Wren has a breast and sides colored warm brown-buff, not a sharply pale belly-and-throat pattern.
Winter Wren shows undertail coverts with bold dark barring.
Winter Wren has a crown and nape that are brown and subtly barred rather than strongly striped.
Winter Wren shows a rounded head with no bold head stripes.
Winter Wren has scapulars marked with dark bars on a rusty-brown base.
Winter Wren shows a barred rump that continues the heavy patterning of the back.
Winter Wren has wing coverts edged warm brown, adding to a finely patterned wing surface.
Winter Wren shows tertials with dark bars and warm brown edges.
Winter Wren has a uniformly dark, richly colored back without the plainer open look of House Wren.
Winter Wren shows flanks that are rich brown with heavy black barring.
Winter Wren has a pale belly that is only slightly lighter than the breast, not strongly contrasting.
Winter Wren shows a plain face lacking the dark eye line and bright eyebrow contrast typical of Marsh Wren.
Winter Wren has no bold black-and-white facial pattern like Marsh Wren.
Winter Wren shows a darker, richer body color than Marsh Wren, which looks paler and more contrasty in the face.
Winter Wren has a shorter-looking tail than Carolina Wren, giving a stubbier rear end.
Winter Wren shows a more heavily barred body overall than Carolina Wren, especially on wings, tail, and flanks.
Winter Wren has a more uniformly dark brown face than Bewick Wren, without a bright white eyebrow dominating the head.
Winter Wren shows warmer, darker underparts than the cleaner pale underparts of Bewick Wren.
Winter Wren has a small, compact silhouette that looks denser and shorter-bodied than House Wren.
Winter Wren shows dense fine vermiculation on the upperparts, strengthening the dark textured look.
Winter Wren has an overall richly barred rufous-brown appearance that is darker and more patterned than House Wren, Carolina Wren, Marsh Wren, or Bewick Wren.

Common Yellowthroat has a fairly long rounded tail.
Common Yellowthroat has dark legs and feet.

Common Yellowthroat shows a yellow throat and upper breast rather than an all-yellow underbody like many Hooded Warblers.
